text:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle in quantum mechanics can be understood by comparing it to trying to take a sharp, high-resolution photograph of a fast-moving car at night. If you use a very fast shutter speed to freeze the car's exact position (pinpointing position), the image becomes dark and blurry, making it impossible to determine how fast the car was moving (momentum). Conversely, if you use a slower shutter speed to capture the streak of light and determine the speed, the car's precise location within that streak becomes fuzzy. You cannot have perfect clarity on both the exact location and the exact speed simultaneously.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
